subproblem.title: Support of a cone over a current supported in a closed ball
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, R ∈ ℝ, X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ m and C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1) with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) and Cone(X, C), i.e. C(ω) = X(ψ) whenever ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) and ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x in some open set N ⊇ spt X and all v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m ((x, v) := Fin.cons x v). Then spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), X.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → C ω = X ψ) → C.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof. In Step 2 the radius δ of the neighbourhood B_{R+δ}(0) on which ω vanishes is here given explicitly (δ := r), so no compactness or thickening argument is needed.
Notation: D^k(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ k. For C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1), spt C = univ ∖ zeroRegion(C), where zeroRegion(C) is the union of all sets W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ univ, and C vanishes on W, i.e. C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
1. Let p ∈ spt C and suppose, for contradiction, that p ∉ B̄_R(0), i.e. ‖p‖ > R. Put r := (‖p‖ − R)/2 > 0 and W := B_r(p).
2. W is open; since r ≠ 0, closure W = B̄_r(p) (closure_ball), which is compact (closed balls of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P are compact), and closure W ⊆ univ.
3. Claim: C vanishes on W. Let ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Put N := B_{R+r}(0), an open set; since r > 0, spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ B_{R+r}(0) = N (closedBall_subset_ball). Let x ∈ N, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m and t ∈ [0, 1]. Then ‖tx‖ = t‖x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ < R + r. If tx belonged to tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(p), then ‖tx − p‖ < r and ‖p‖ ≤ ‖tx‖ + ‖tx − p‖ < (R + r) + r = ‖p‖, which is absurd. Hence tx ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(tx) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and t^m·ω(tx)(x, v) = 0. The integrand therefore vanishes on [0, 1] = uIcc 0 1, and intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt = ∫_0^1 0 dt = 0 = 0(x)(v). So ψ := 0 ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) satisfies ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ N and all v, where N is open and N ⊇ spt X. By Cone(X, C), C(ω) = X(0) = 0, since X is linear.
4. By Steps 2 and 3, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion(C), and p ∈ W because ‖p − p‖ = 0 < r. Thus p ∈ zeroRegion(C), contradicting p ∈ spt C = univ ∖ zeroRegion(C). Hence every p ∈ spt C lies in B̄_R(0), i.e. spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0). (The argument uses no sign condition on R: if R < 0 the same steps apply verbatim.) ∎
proof_key_steps: For p with ‖p‖ > R set r := (‖p‖ − R)/2 > 0 and W := B_r(p), which is open with compact closure B̄_r(p) ⊆ univ.
If tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tx ∉ tsupport ω for x ∈ B_{R+r}(0) and t ∈ [0, 1], so ψ := 0 satisfies the radial formula on the open N := B_{R+r}(0) ⊇ spt X and Cone(X, C) gives C(ω) = X(0) = 0.
Thus W lies in zeroRegion(C) and contains p, contradicting p ∈ spt C; hence spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).

audit.reason: The inline cone predicate exactly matches the prose. The compact-neighborhood argument places each hypothetical exterior support point in the zero region, using the zero test form and the stated triangle inequality. The proof also covers negative R, including an empty formula neighborhood, so no omitted nonnegativity assumption is needed.

subproblem.title: Mass comparison through bounded transfer test forms
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ n, C ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k and c, R ∈ ℝ with c ≥ 0, R ≥ 0 and M(X) < ∞. Assume that for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ (a test k-form with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y) and every δ > 0 there is ψ ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n with C(ω) = X(ψ) and covectorEuclideanNorm(ψ(x)) ≤ c·(R + δ) for all x. Then M(C) ≤ ofReal(c·R)·M(X).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) k) (c R : ℝ), 0 ≤ c → 0 ≤ R → X.mass < ∞ → (∀ ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) k univ, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, C ω = X ψ ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ c * (R + δ)) → C.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * R) * X.mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof (the mass bound), with the construction of the transfer forms ψ = ζ_δψ_ω abstracted into the hypothesis.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ j, M(T) := T.mass = T.massOn univ = sSup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j univ} ∈ [0, ∞], where ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j univ means ω ∈ TestFormOn univ j, tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
1. Since M(X) < ∞, B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0 satisfies M(X) = ofReal(B) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
2. Fix ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ. Claim: C(ω) ≤ cR·B. Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(Bc + 1). As B, c ≥ 0 we have Bc + 1 > 0, δ > 0 and δ(Bc + 1) = ε, hence Bcδ = ε − δ < ε. By hypothesis there is ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ n with C(ω) = X(ψ) and |ψ(x)| ≤ c(R + δ) for all x. Apply the accepted lemma cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (sibling mass_bound) with U = W = univ, T = X, the form ψ, the bound B (B ≥ 0 and X.massOn univ = M(X) = ofReal B), tsupport ψ ⊆ univ, and the pointwise bound c(R + δ): |X(ψ)| ≤ B·c(R + δ). Hence C(ω) = X(ψ) ≤ |X(ψ)| ≤ cRB + Bcδ < cRB + ε. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, C(ω) ≤ cRB (le_of_forall_pos_lt_add).
3. By monotonicity of ofReal and since cR ≥ 0: ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ ofReal(cR·B) = ofReal(cR)·ofReal(B) = ofReal(cR)·M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul).
4. M(C) = C.massOn univ is the supremum of ofReal(C(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ, and by Step 3 each of these values is ≤ ofReal(cR)·M(X). Hence M(C) ≤ ofReal(c·R)·M(X) (sSup_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write M(X) = ofReal B with B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0.
For admissible ω and δ = ε/(Bc + 1), the hypothesis and cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le give C(ω) = X(ψ) ≤ Bc(R + δ) < cRB + ε; hence C(ω) ≤ cRB.
ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ ofReal(cR)·ofReal(B) = ofReal(cR)·M(X); taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(C) ≤ ofReal(cR)·M(X).

audit.reason: The transfer-form hypothesis and all nonnegativity and finiteness assumptions match the Lean type. Finite mass justifies conversion to B = M(X).toReal; the explicit positive δ gives the limiting evaluation bound. ofReal multiplication and the defining supremum then yield precisely the claimed mass inequality, using only mass_bound.

subproblem.title: Coefficient-norm bound for the radial integral
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let ω : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be any (m+1)-form (DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m+1); no regularity is assumed) with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for every y ∈ ℝ^P, let x ∈ ℝ^P, and let β ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) be an m-covector with β(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m, where (x, v) := Fin.cons x v and the integral is the interval integral over [0, 1]. Then covectorEuclideanNorm(β) ≤ P^{2m+1}·‖x‖.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (x : Eucl P) (β : Covector (Eucl P) m), (∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω y) ≤ 1) → (∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, β v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ (2 * m + 1) * ‖x‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4 and 5 of the parent proof (coefficient estimate and pointwise bound), stated for an arbitrary covector β given by the radial integral at one point x.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for a covector α on ℝ^P; e_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ a for a ∈ Fin P (the standard orthonormal basis, so ‖e_a‖ = 1); for I : Fin m → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(m)}); (x, u) := Fin.cons x u. Put K := P^{m+1}‖x‖ ≥ 0.
1. (Coefficient estimate.) Let α ∈ Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and u ∈ (ℝ^P)^m with ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1 for all i. Then |α(x, u)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α|.
 (a) If x = 0, the tuple (x, u) has the zero vector in slot 0, so α(x, u) = 0 by multilinearity (map_coord_zero), and 0 ≤ P^{m+1}·0·|α|.
 (b) If x ≠ 0, then ‖x‖ > 0. Let τ := (‖x‖⁻¹x, u) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}. Then ‖τ_0‖ = ‖x‖⁻¹‖x‖ = 1 and ‖τ_{i+1}‖ = ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1 for all i. The tuple (x, u) is τ with its slot 0 replaced by ‖x‖·τ_0 (because ‖x‖·(‖x‖⁻¹x) = x), so linearity of α in slot 0 (map_update_smul) gives α(x, u) = ‖x‖·α(τ). The accepted lemma isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le (sibling covector_bound, with n := m+1) gives |α(τ)| ≤ P^{m+1}|α|. Hence |α(x, u)| = ‖x‖·|α(τ)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α|.
2. (Each coordinate value of β.) Fix I : Fin m → Fin P and let f(t) := t^m·ω(tx)(x, e_I). For t ∈ Ι(0, 1) = (0, 1] we have 0 ≤ t^m ≤ 1 and |ω(tx)| ≤ 1 by hypothesis, and Step 1 with α := ω(tx) and u := e_I (every ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = 1) gives |ω(tx)(x, e_I)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|ω(tx)| ≤ K. Hence |f(t)| ≤ 1·K = K for all t ∈ (0, 1]. By the interval-integral bound ‖∫_a^b f‖ ≤ C·|b − a| whenever ‖f(t)‖ ≤ C for all t ∈ Ι(a, b) (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, which needs no integrability hypothesis because the integral of a non-integrable function is 0), |β(e_I)| = |∫_0^1 f(t) dt| ≤ K·|1 − 0| = K. Consequently β(e_I)² = |β(e_I)|² ≤ K².
3. (Summation.) By definition |β| = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin P} s_I), where s_I := β(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and s_I := 0 otherwise. By Step 2, 0 ≤ s_I ≤ K² for every I, and there are exactly P^m maps I : Fin m → Fin P (Fintype.card_fun). Since sqrt is monotone, |β| ≤ sqrt(P^m·K²). The natural number N := P^m satisfies N ≤ N² (Nat.le_self_pow; N = 0 or N ≥ 1), so P^m·K² ≤ (P^m)²·K² = (P^m·K)² and sqrt(P^m·K²) ≤ sqrt((P^m·K)²) = P^m·K, because P^m·K ≥ 0. Finally P^m·K = P^m·P^{m+1}‖x‖ = P^{2m+1}‖x‖. Hence covectorEuclideanNorm(β) ≤ P^{2m+1}‖x‖. (No case distinction on P is needed: for P = 0 the bound K = 0 forces every term to vanish.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Coefficient estimate |α(x, u)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α| for ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1: zero if x = 0, otherwise α(x, u) = ‖x‖·α(‖x‖⁻¹x, u) and the reused isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le.
For every I : Fin m → Fin P, |β(e_I)| ≤ K := P^{m+1}‖x‖ by the constant bound for interval integrals, using 0 ≤ t^m ≤ 1 and |ω(tx)| ≤ 1.
|β|² is a sum over the P^m maps I of terms in [0, K²]; sqrt(P^m K²) ≤ P^m K = P^{2m+1}‖x‖ since P^m ≤ (P^m)².

audit.reason: The type faithfully includes the absence of regularity assumptions. Normalizing the first argument, applying covector_bound, using the integrability-free constant interval-integral bound, and summing coefficient squares prove the exact estimate. The cardinality argument handles P = 0 and m = 0. Only the declared dependency is used.

subproblem.title: Smooth cutoff of the radial form to a bounded test form
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let ω : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be any (m+1)-form, let ψ₀ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) be a C^∞ m-form (ContDiff ℝ ∞) with ψ₀(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m ((x, v) := Fin.cons x v), and let 0 < r < s. Then there is a test form ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ m such that (i) ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for every x in the open ball B_r(0) and every v, and (ii) if covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for every y, then covectorEuclideanNorm(ψ(x)) ≤ P^{2m+1}·s for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (ψ₀ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) (r s : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ₀ → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), ψ₀ x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → 0 < r → r < s → ∃ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m, (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Eucl P) r, ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) ∧ ((∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω y) ≤ 1) → ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ (2 * m + 1) * s)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 0 of the parent proof (ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω is a test form satisfying the radial formula on B_r(0)) and the pointwise part of Step 6 (|ζψ_ω(x)| ≤ c·s), with the smooth radial form ψ_ω supplied as the input ψ₀.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; B_ρ(0), B̄_ρ(0) are the open and closed balls; D^m(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ m, whose elements are the m-forms f : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) that are C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞), have compact support, and satisfy tsupport f ⊆ univ.
1. (Bump function.) Since 0 < r < s and Eucl P is a finite-dimensional inner product space (so it carries smooth bump functions), there is a ContDiffBump ζ centred at 0 with rIn = r and rOut = s. Its coercion ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), satisfies 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), ζ(x) = 1 for x ∈ B̄_r(0) (one_of_mem_closedBall), support ζ = B_s(0) (support_eq), and has compact support (hasCompactSupport).
2. (The test form.) Define f(x) := ζ(x)·ψ₀(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P). f is C^∞ as the product of the C^∞ scalar function ζ and the C^∞ form ψ₀ (ContDiff.smul), it has compact support because ζ has (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport f ⊆ univ trivially. Hence f ∈ D^m(ℝ^P); let ψ be f regarded as an element of TestFormOn univ m.
3. (Property (i).) Let x ∈ B_r(0) and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Then x ∈ B̄_r(0), so ζ(x) = 1 and ψ(x)(v) = ψ₀(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt by the hypothesis on ψ₀.
4. (Homogeneity.) For a ∈ ℝ and α ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P): (aα)(e_I) = a·α(e_I) for every coordinate tuple e_I, so the sum of squares S' defining |aα|² equals a² times the sum S defining |α|², and |aα| = sqrt(a²·S) = |a|·sqrt(S) = |a|·|α| (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
5. (Property (ii).) Assume |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y and let x ∈ ℝ^P. By Step 4, |ψ(x)| = |ζ(x)|·|ψ₀(x)|.
 (a) If ‖x‖ < s: |ζ(x)| = ζ(x) ≤ 1. The covector β := ψ₀(x) satisfies β(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all v, so the sibling lemma iwl_cr_cest_radial_coeff_bound gives |ψ₀(x)| ≤ P^{2m+1}‖x‖. Hence |ψ(x)| ≤ 1·P^{2m+1}‖x‖ ≤ P^{2m+1}·s.
 (b) If ‖x‖ ≥ s: x ∉ B_s(0) = support ζ, so ζ(x) = 0 and |ψ(x)| = 0 ≤ P^{2m+1}·s, as s > r > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the ContDiffBump ζ centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = s; ψ := ζψ₀ is C^∞ with compact support, i.e. an element of TestFormOn univ m.
